<Rep. Joseph D. Morelle>: Opposition to H.R. 9368
Committee Democrats oppose H.R. 9368 because it would functionally eviscerate mail voting, needlessly burden millions of eligible American voters, and furthers President Trump's obsession with undermining the security and integrity of American elections in aid of Republican politicians.
The voter identification regime proposed in H.R. 9368 would be more restrictive than any identification system currently in use across the country, including in states like Texas and Florida. Like the SAVE America Act, this bill would require voters to submit copies of a severely limited list of photo identification alongside their mail ballot--a provision so extreme the Republican Lieutenant Governor of Utah noted it could violate ``the Constitutional right to a secret ballot.''\1\ Indeed, Republican Governor of Ohio Mike DeWine recently vetoed a similar state proposal to require Ohioans to surrender copies of photo identification alongside their mail ballots, noting that such restrictions ``would not discourage fraud, would not add any real security, and would create an additional and significant burden for Ohioans who vote by mail.''
\1\Alarmingly, H.R. 9368--as amended at the Committee's June 24, 2026, markup--would allow voters to escape this photocopy requirement if they cast their mail ballot alongside ``a notarization by a notary public attesting that the individual has personally marked the ballot,'' requiring voters without identification to mark their private ballot in view of a notary public.
Further, the bill would bar American citizens from casting a ballot in person unless they presented one of a limited list of identification documents: (1) a valid state-issued motor vehicle driver's license that includes a photo of the individual and an expiration date; (2) a valid state-issued photo identification card with an expiration date; (3) a valid U.S. passport; (4) a valid photo identification issued by the Department of Defense or the Department of Veterans Affairs; or
(5) a valid Tribal identification that includes a photo and an expiration date, despite the fact that many Tribal IDs do not feature expiration dates. It would not allow many forms of identification currently used in states across the nation-- including student IDs, hunting and firearm licenses, fishing licenses, or employee identification cards.
To be clear, Committee Democrats support voter identification, but H.R. 9368 is not a voter identification bill--it is a voter suppression bill. Voter identification standards, when fully accessible and non-discriminatory, are some of the many effective election integrity tools available to election administrators. In New York, for instance, voters are required to prove their identity when registering to vote or casting their first ballot, after which the state relies on a dependable signature matching regime. This is a secure, reliable system.
Unfortunately, H.R. 9368--the Voter ID Act--fails to grasp this reality. As with other pieces of strikingly similar legislation introduced by congressional Republicans this Congress--including the SAVE Act, the SAVE America Act, and the Make Elections Great Again Act--this bill is a bad-faith solution in search of an imaginary problem. It is another step taken in congressional Republicans' long march, at the heels of President Trump, to sow distrust in our federal elections and spread long-debunked conspiracy theories about voting to the American people.
In contrast to these restrictive, suppressive efforts, Committee Democrats continue to proudly champion the Freedom to Vote Act (``FTVA''), which includes a strong voter identification provision. The FTVA sets uniform, accessible identification standards, granting flexibility to states to choose specific requirements. Among the allowable IDs under the FTVA are a driver's license or other state-issued ID, a passport, an employee identification card, a student ID, a military ID, a gun license, a hunting or fishing license, and several other secure options.
Committee Democrats offered this provision as an amendment to H.R. 9368--an amendment that, in the spirit of good-faith bipartisanship, maintained a Republican grantmaking provision included in the underlying H.R. 9368. Unfortunately, Committee Republicans appear disinterested in good-faith cooperation-- they voted down this compromise measure in a party-line vote. They are interested in appeasing the leader of their party, whose childlike fixation on conspiracy theories and preoccupation with suppressing American voting power is endangering both the crucial business of this House--as evidenced by the collapse of Speaker Johnson's control of the floor--and Republicans' standing with the American electorate. For those reasons, Committee Democrats strongly oppose H.R. 9368, the Voter ID Act.
Joseph D. Morelle,
Ranking Member.
